facts.text: Slade Craven is played by John Mann, a real-life frontman of Canadian folk-rock band Spirit of the West. Wikipedia says this was his first and only leading role.
The tagline promised: One killer. Forty hostages. Ten million internet viewers.
This was the last movie released by Trimark Pictures.
Craig Sheffer led both this film and Turbulence 2: Fear of Flying, but played a different character in each one.
Monika Schnarre won the Ford Supermodel of the World contest at 14, and at 15 she was the youngest ever in the Sports Illustrated swimsuit issue.
Gabrielle Anwar once held the record as the World's Fastest Talker, set at a Guinness World Records exhibit in London while she was still at drama school.
Joe Mantegna co-starred with Ray Liotta, star of the original Turbulence, in The Rat Pack (1998). Years later he'd play an FBI agent on Criminal Minds from 2007 to 2020.
Red Letter Media put this on Best of the Worst and crowned it the winner of the episode for being the most entertaining of the bunch.
Filmed in Vancouver, British Columbia, standing in for Los Angeles and a Boeing 747 flight to Toronto.
John Mann was diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer's at 50 and went public in 2014. Spirit of the West played their last show two years later.
Monika Schnarre traveled behind the Iron Curtain in 1987 to help launch Burda Moden, the first fashion magazine published in the Soviet Union.
Gabrielle Anwar tangoed with Al Pacino in Scent of a Woman (1992), the role that made her famous.
The film's songs include Razor Electric and Gun Love, performed by Mann as Slade Craven. Other tracks come from the bands thickliquid and Deathbyday.
Rutger Hauer and John Mann both died in 2019, Hauer on July 19 and Mann on November 20.
Gabrielle Anwar and Rutger Hauer played opposite each other again a year later in Flying Virus.
Later cult-movie shows kept the film alive: it's referenced in Hologram Man, Faust, and Blood Street (2018) and in Merry Kick-mas! (2017).
